title: add-jsonschema-strict-mode-response-format-openai-compat
author: Asha Patel
description: Context: introduce a first-class JSON Schema structured output mode on the Redwood API to improve developer ergonomics and OpenAI compatibility. Motivation: teams need a way to require models to produce strongly-typed JSON responses, get clear validation errors, and optionally enforce strict schemas that reject extra fields. This PR adds response_format:json_schema support, server-side schema validation, improved error messages for both validation and strict-mode failures, an OpenAI-compat compatibility layer for existing clients, and docs + tests. Changes include: 1) API surface: response_format parameter accepts {type: "json_schema", schema: <JSON Schema>, strict: true|false, on_validation_error: "error"|"warn"} 2) Runtime validator that validates streaming tokens against a permissive incremental parser and final strict validation on completion 3) Error reporting: structured validation error object returned in the API error response and surfaced in logs with trace IDs 4) Compatibility shim: when openai_compat flag is set we translate schema errors into OpenAI-style error codes and messages 5) Docs: examples and migration guide added to redwood-docs 6) Tests: unit & integration coverage for permissive and strict modes. Backwards compatibility: default behavior unchanged (response_format omitted continues to return free-form text). Checklist: [x] API contract and serializer changes [x] runtime validator + incremental parser [x] OpenAI compatibility mapping [x] unit tests [x] integration tests with streaming [x] docs + examples [x] release notes
commits_summary: a) Add server-side jsonschema validator + incremental streaming parser; b) Add API parsing and response_format handling; c) Map validation errors to openai_compat error shapes; d) Add tests and docs; e) Fix flaky streaming case for partial-object tokens
review_comments: Miguel: requested clearer error message shapes and suggested error codes for openai_compat mapping; also asked for an example of how streaming partial objects are handled. Asha: added an incremental parser to accept chunks and added a final strict validation step; updated error object schema to include 'path', 'expected', 'received', and 'hint'. Priya: requested extra unit tests for nested arrays and requested that strict mode be opt-in; author responded that strict defaults to false and is opt-in, and added tests. Ethan: approved after minor docs wording nits were fixed. CI initially showed a flaky streaming e2e failure which was traced to parser buffer handling; fix included in a follow-up commit.
release_notes: - New response_format 'json_schema' with optional 'strict' boolean to enforce schema. - Server-side validation with clear structured errors (path, expected, received, hint). - OpenAI compatibility mode maps validation errors to OpenAI-style error codes for easier migration. - Streaming-friendly incremental parser with final strict validation. - Backward compatible: default behavior unchanged.
tests: added unit tests for incremental parser and validator
added integration tests for streaming + strict mode
error_examples: ValidationError: response failed final schema validation at /items/0/name: expected string but got number
StrictModeError: response contained unexpected property 'extra_info' which is disallowed in strict mode
StreamingParseError: incomplete JSON fragment after timeout; final validation failed
notes_for_ops: Rollout: feature is behind flag 'enable_jsonschema_response_format' and off by default for hosted customers. Dedicated customers may opt-in in their config. Telemetry: validation.failures and validation.strict_violation metrics added. In case of spike, ops can toggle the feature flag or set on_validation_error to 'warn' as a mitigation.
examples: Python: response = client.generate(prompt, response_format={"type":"json_schema", "schema": my_schema, "strict": True})
OpenAI-compat: pass openai_compat=True and we'll return 'type':'invalid_response' style errors when validation fails
notes: Follow-ups: improve reparsing heuristics for extremely large streaming responses; add schema caching for common schemas to reduce CPU cost; add opt-in automated corrective reasks for minor shape mismatches
